About: Hardware target profiles (HardwareBudget). Pick one in Project Settings > Hardware. A project's Assets/Config/HardwareProfiles.json adds profiles, replaces one with the same Name, or starts from one with "Extends". Missing keys and 0 mean no limit. Memory is in MiB; Caps are what the target can do, applied when the profile is enforced. The figures are budgets for a game on that machine, not its hardware maximums. QualityPresets are the player's graphics levels (PlayerSettings Graphics.Quality): Caps in the same shape, replaced by Name or started with "Extends" the same way; under an enforced profile the stricter cap wins.

Profiles.Name: 2004 PC
Profiles.Description: A high-end PC of 2004 (Half-Life 2, Doom 3, Far Cry): Pentium 4 or Athlon 64, 1 GB of RAM, a GeForce 6800 or Radeon X800 with 256 MB.

Profiles.Name: Xbox 360
Profiles.Description: Microsoft's 2005 console: three 3.2 GHz PowerPC cores, 512 MB of unified GDDR3 (about 480 MB for games), the Xenos GPU with 10 MB of eDRAM. Most games ran at 30 fps at 720p or below.

Profiles.Name: Switch
Profiles.Description: Nintendo Switch (2017): four 1 GHz Cortex-A57 cores, 4 GB of unified LPDDR4 (about 3.2 GB for games), a 256-core Maxwell GPU. 720p handheld, usually 30 fps.

Profiles.Name: Steam Deck
Profiles.Description: Valve's 2022 handheld: a 4-core Zen 2 APU, 16 GB of unified LPDDR5, an RDNA 2 GPU (1.6 TFLOPS) driving 1280x800. Deck Verified asks for 30 fps.

QualityPresets.Name: Low
QualityPresets.Description: Older and integrated GPUs: no volumetric fog, ambient occlusion, depth of field or temporal AA; 1024 shadows and 1024 textures.

QualityPresets.Name: Medium
QualityPresets.Description: Mid-range GPUs: everything on, with 2048 shadows and textures and a coarser volumetric fog.

QualityPresets.Name: High
QualityPresets.Description: Everything on; shadows up to 4096 and volumetric fog up to 64 steps.

QualityPresets.Name: Ultra
QualityPresets.Description: No player caps: what the scenes ask for.
